text: Great sesh, fam. Real ones come to office hours.
note: A soft, gentle whisper right into the mic, proud of saying fam; the room's PA makes it boom. Say 'real ones' clearly.
Whispered, warm, delighted, into the mic. Clean read, exactly these words.
Barely moving his lips, low, certain, like a funeral.

text: It says hours. Plural. That's a suggestion.
note: Easy, packing up, completely sure, a little amused.
Flat, quiet, like a warning.
Light, curious.
A beat of unease, then brisk, changing the subject, leaving. Say every word clearly, including the last word, five.
Flat, under his breath, refusing what he sees. Long cut only.

text: I did not RSVP to that.
note: Quiet, betrayed, offended, stressing RSVP.

text: Just go in, baby. It's faster.
note: Warm older woman, unbothered, mopping, not looking up.
Very calm, kind, slow, soft.
Insisting, a little too fast, still sure he is leaving.
Nodding, kind, completely at peace.

text: Did they ever drop the new GTA?
note: Gentle, hopeful, like it's nothing.
Soft, kind, he cannot do it to him.
Delighted, warm, still soft, no mic now.
Nervous, gentle, soft.
Very small, hopeful and scared of the answer, his lip trembling.
Soft, a beat of giving in; he cannot say no to this man.
A whisper, moved to tears, overwhelmed.
Hopeful, bright, soft.
Normal, a bit annoyed, on the pitch.

A soft, gentle whisper right into the mic, warm and delighted, as if inviting him to a party; the room's PA makes it boom. Say every word clearly, including the last word, today.
Calm and low to his friend, a clear even read, and the last word, five, is said fully and clearly, not swallowed.

text: Nio! Can you swing by my office hours after class? It won't take a minute.
note: Warm, booming whisper through a lecture-hall mic. Say the name exactly as NEE-oh, short and bright, not Neil.

text: He picked you. I go every week. He has a candle.
note: Gasping, thrilled and sincere, grabbing her friend's arm, whispering fast in class. Say candle clearly.

text: Maya. The final's at five. If I'm not on that pitch, we forfeit.
note: Low and calm but firm, whispering in class. Every word clear; the word five is said fully and stressed.
Bright and pleading, cheerful, a little too loud for class.

text: That's how they get you. It's one minute, then you're forty, and it's still office hours.
note: Deadpan, low and certain, a confident wrong theory delivered like common knowledge. Say forty clearly.
Flat, amused, completely unbothered.

text: In a world... where one minute... is forever.
note: A deep, slow, dramatic movie trailer voice, very serious, long pauses between phrases.
A deep, slow, dramatic movie trailer voice, ominous, the last word always held.

text: Did you just do a trailer?
note: Staring at him, flat and baffled, a dry question.
Brisk and decided, getting up, quietly. Start straight on the first word, I'm, with no sound before it.
Delighted, bouncing up, sincere.
Dreamy and happy, sincere, like admiring a garden.

text: It's the trailer. We're in the trailer.
note: Rattled but deadpan, low and fast, staring at his phone.
Light, kind and dismissive, skipping along.
Calm and kind, not looking up from her mop, as if stating the weather.
Lighting up, warm and chatty, greeting an old friend in a coffee shop. Say Darnell clearly.
Warm, slow and very calm, content.

text: How long have you been next?
note: Quiet, flat and slow, a deadpan question, already suspecting the answer.
Gentle and peaceful after giving up counting, like it is completely normal. Say every word clearly.
Sincere and encouraging, completely missing the point.
Beaming, warm, delighted, in a doorway. Say the name Nio crisply, NEE-oh.
Very small and quiet, hopeful, almost a whisper, bracing for a no.
A soft beat, then kind and sincere, a small real moment.
Stunned and quiet, staring past his friend at something impossible.
Calm, laid back, a little smug, dropping the ball for kick-off. Say every word clearly.
